kevin: quick canary run on canary-cluster-3. saw tail blow up after we set a more aggressive max_wait_ms for continuous batching. posting findings + config. @eng-runtime :eyes:

kevin: summary: p50 ~38ms, p95 jumped from 110ms -> 260ms, p99 from 320ms -> 720ms after changing max_wait_ms=12 -> 6 (ms). throughput up ~7% but unacceptable tail. KV cache hit ratio fell from 91% -> 70% (weird).

kevin: config diff we rolled: ```json
{
  "max_batch_tokens": 2048,
  "max_wait_ms": 6,
  "microbatch_target_tokens": 64,
  "kv_cache_enabled": true,
  "kernel_fallback": "auto"
}
```

maria: thanks — good catch. two quick hypotheses: 1) shrinking max_wait_ms increases microbatch churn (more small batches), which reduces prefetched KV reuse and moves more work to kernel fallback paths; 2) the scheduler may be flushing partial microbatches more often, increasing tail due to extra scheduling hops.

alex: +1 to maria. we saw similar in perf lab when max_wait_ms <= 8 with small seq len workloads. kernel_fallback auto path does a runtime probe that can add ~1-2ms per request when state changes (hot kernel -> quantized kernel). if microbatches flip kernels frequently the overhead accumulates at tail.

luca: idea: try raising max_batch_tokens to give more room for aggregation while keeping max_wait_ms low-ish. e.g. max_batch_tokens=4096, max_wait_ms=8, microbatch_target_tokens=128. that gives better batching without blowing avg latency too much. also add a short warmup window for kernel selection so we only probe fallback on first few batches per machine-lifecycle.

kevin: FYI KV hit drop looked correlated: when we observed smaller batches the prefix KV lifetime was shorter (eviction threshold hit). On the canary pod we had frequent eviction spikes in kv-lru metrics. logs: ```
KV_EVICT count=87 window=60s
KV_HIT_RATE 0.70
KV_PREFETCH_MISS 0.18
```

maria: try enabling prefix-retention tweak (kv_prefetch_retention_ms = 3000) for the canary and re-run. also capture per-request kernel tag so we can see how often fallback triggers.

alex: for immediate troubleshooting, run a two-arm A/B on the canary: arm A = max_wait_ms=6, max_batch_tokens=2048 (current), arm B = max_wait_ms=8, max_batch_tokens=4096, both with microbatch_target_tokens bumped to 96. measure p95/p99, kv_hit_ratio, and kernel_fallback_rate.

kevin: running that now. attaching the perf probe script I used: ```bash
# run perf sweep
python infra/tools/latency_sweep.py --cluster canary-cluster-3 \
  --duration 15m --qps 120 --input dist=short-seqs.json \
  --report /tmp/sweep.json
```

sre-bot: perf dashboard: https://dash.internal.redwood/runtime/canary-cluster-3?range=30m — current snapshot shows the p99 spikes line up with KV_EVICT spikes and kernel_switch events.

luca: another knob: backpressure-aware enqueue. if in-flight queue > 60% of max_batch_tokens, prefer flush earliest batch instead of waiting. reduces head-of-line blocking for long requests. can implement as scheduler override with low risk.

maria: note on SLOs: product wants p95 < 140ms for interactive tier. our current arm A fails, arm B might pass but we need to watch p99. aim: keep p95 <= 140ms and not degrade throughput >5%.

ops-bot: rolling ab test: arm B will be routed to 10% of canary hosts at 1956789180. monitor will auto rollback if p95 > 200ms or errors >1%.

kevin: logged results after 15m: arm A (baseline) p95=260ms p99=720ms kv_hit=0.70 throughput=128rps; arm B p95=132ms p99=310ms kv_hit=0.88 throughput=122rps. kernel_fallback_rate dropped from 0.09 -> 0.012.

kevin: takeaways: small max_wait_ms + small max_batch_tokens -> microbursting that kills KV reuse and causes kernel churn and long tails. increasing max_batch_tokens + modest wait is best tradeoff for this workload.

maria: great. next steps: 1) promote arm B defaults for interactive tier on canary, 2) implement short kernel warmup suppression, 3) add kv_prefetch_retention_ms toggle, 4) add scheduler backpressure heuristic. i'll file infra tickets.

alex: also add per-model rollout flag so models with very short context (chat prompts) can use a lower max_wait_ms safely.

kevin: I'll open the change PR with the new defaults and perf artifacts. thanks all :thumbsup:
